Answer: A
Reason: Intralobar pulmonary sequestration typically presents as a mass in the lower lobe (most commonly left) that lacks communication with the tracheobronchial tree and receives systemic arterial supply, distinguishing it from other lung pathologies. The provided CT image shows a left-sided lower lobe opacity consistent with this presentation, while the 3D reconstruction highlights the aberrant systemic vasculature characteristic of sequestration.
